spatial_claims.claim: Cone has circular base ABCD and apex E; cylinder has same base ABCD and equal height h
Square ABCD is inscribed in circle ABCD; inscribed square is greater than half the circle
Inscribed polygon P obtained by successive arc bisection lies inside circle; circle - area(P) < S
Prism on polygon P with height h is inscribed in the cylinder
Pyramid with base P and apex E is inscribed in the cone
cylinder - prism(P) equals the solid above the circular segments between P and the circle, at the same height
Polygon P decomposed into triangles T_i; prism on P decomposes into prisms on T_i; pyramid on P decomposes into pyramids on T_i
Each triangular prism on T_i decomposes into three equal pyramids (by 12.7); these have the same height as pyramid(T_i, E); so prism(T_i) = 3 * pyramid(T_i, E)
pyramid(P, E) is inscribed in the cone, so cone > pyramid(P, E)
Circumscribed polygon Q about circle obtained by tangent lines; area(Q) - circle < S
Prism on Q circumscribes the cylinder; pyramid(Q, E) circumscribes the cone
Cone is inscribed in pyramid(Q, E), so pyramid(Q, E) > cone

configuration_map: 3D configuration: Base plane contains circle ABCD. Apex E is at the top of the cone at height h above the center of the circle. Cylinder extends from circle ABCD upward to height h. In Case 1: Inscribed polygon P lies inside circle ABCD in the base plane. Prism(P) extends from P upward to height h, entirely contained within the cylinder. Pyramid(P,E) connects base P to apex E, entirely contained within the cone. Each triangle T_i of P generates a triangular prism of height h (inside the cylinder's prism) and a pyramid to E (inside the cone's pyramid). In Case 2: Circumscribed polygon Q contains circle ABCD in the base plane. Prism(Q) extends from Q upward to height h, containing the cylinder. Pyramid(Q,E) connects base Q to apex E, containing the cone. Throughout: E remains at fixed height h above center; P stays inside circle; Q stays outside circle. Heights of all prisms and pyramids equal h (the common height of cone and cylinder).
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The inscribed/circumscribed containment relationships (polygon inside/outside circle implies solid inside/outside cone/cylinder) are geometrically correct and compatible with each other. The height equality (cone height = cylinder height = prism height = pyramid height) is maintained consistently throughout. The decomposition of prisms into pyramids via 12.7 and the volume comparison via 12.5 are applied in a spatially valid manner. No angle decompositions, no interior/exterior point arguments, and no ray ordering claims appear -- the primary error patterns from the protocol do not apply to this volumetric method-of-exhaustion proof.
